title: Occupancy and Residency Certification — Standing Date of a Mailed Certification Form
content:
**Rule.** Under the Occupancy and Residency Certification product, a mailed certification form's standing date is the form's anchor date where every standing limit is met, and the signature date the form states otherwise.

**Standing limits.** Every standing limit is met when:

1. the calendar days from the form's signature date to the anchor date are no more than the pre-return window;
2. the calendar days from the form's signature date to its receipt are no more than the receipt lag limit; and
3. the due date the profile shows falls on or after the anchor date by no more than the crediting window.

Under the standard rule the anchor date is the signature date the form states and the pre-return window, the receipt lag limit and the crediting window are each zero days, so the form stands on its signature date.

**The mailed form.** It is the accepted occupancy certification form on file for the profile that came by mail and was received most recently, with the signature date it states and the date it was received, a form received before the signature date it states counting as received on it; where none is on file, the handling date stands in for both. The due date is the one the profile shows. Whole calendar months are counted as anniversaries of the day number, a month being complete only on the same day number of a later month. Where two records share the date a reading is ordered by, the one entered first is read.

## Checking the three limits (hypothetical, symbolic)

| Limit | Measured | Met when |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | signature date to anchor date | days no more than the pre-return window |
| 2 | signature date to receipt | days no more than the receipt lag limit |
| 3 | anchor date to the due date shown | due date on or after the anchor date, by no more than the crediting window |

*Hypothetical case on the standard terms.* A form signed on one day and received four days later: the anchor date is the signature date, limit 1 is met (zero days), limit 2 fails (four days against zero), so the form stands on its signature date.
